screen_flag_dispositions.explanation: French words deux mille six cents on registered Foy pp77–78 mean 2,600; the quote crosses the page boundary and describes the leading marching subset.
Same inspected spelled-out 2,600 passage, now used for command scope. It does not establish whole-army strength or uninterrupted control.
Inspected Foy p106 spells out 8,242 Dupont prisoners and 9,393 under Vedel; 23/24 are handover dates, not fighting-strength moments.
Inspected huit mille on Foy p265 means 8,000, for Loison crossing the Tagus on 25 July; not a 29 July engaged return.
Inspected cinq mille on Foy p268 means 5,000 organized Portuguese/Spanish, expressly excluding the irregular crowd.
Inspected Foy pp320–321: pas dix mille means fewer than 10,000 sabres/bayonets; onze mille cinq cents is 11,500 including noncombatants. Distinct populations.
Toreno quote gives 3,000; the 3,500 comparison is Bodart’s separate bodart-strength claim, not attributed to Toreno.

Saint-Cyr p53 says 7 December was the day after capture, explicitly implying 6 December. The comparison with 5 December is the frozen frame end_date, not an unquoted digit asserted to be on this page. No frame correction.
Inspected quinze mille baionnettes and quinze cents sabres on Saint-Cyr p53 mean about 15,000 bayonets and 1,500 sabres for the relief march, excluding Reille left behind.
Inspected Saint-Cyr p64 spells out about 10,000 plus five [thousand] brought by Vives, making the author’s explicit 15,000 opponent estimate. Interested estimate, not an adjudicated local return.
Printed 14 o 15,000 abbreviates 14,000 or 15,000; the retained p266 image establishes the thousands convention. Subsequent 28,000 and cavalry 1,400 are not added together.
The 11 January date is in the inspected heading of letter 14681 on p195 and the section date map 1809-01-11, not in the short quoted body sentence. Toreno’s 22 January arrival remains separate.
